[9-3-15] Happy September everyone! Weekly thread time!

Ok, so my PotA game is on hold for two weeks due to people traveling and events happening in my town (college football, anyone?).

HotDQ started back up yesterday after a several month hiatus. I'm a level 5 Sun Elf Assassin (hence Broken Rogue). We had to do a pretty lengthy recap to remember everything and where we were. In our group is me, a half-dragon paladin, a half-elf fighter, a halfling bard, and a human wizard. Accompanying us at the start was a dwarf-lady NPC (she's actually a gnome, but I'm stuck on calling her a dwarf-lady. They're all short things, so I don't care much), and a golden stag that is an elven prince that was cursed and we need to change back to an elf. I've named him Kevin. The human in my group named him Sparkletits. I've pledged that Kevin/Sparkletits will be my elf husband after he's changed back. So, we were in Waterdeep, and I found a wizard that can change Kevin/Sparkletits back into an elf, paid the 100 gold to do so, and also bought him a set of fine clothes. Kevin/Sparkletits has no memory of who he is, and wants to go off in search of himself. He did leave me a trinket that he says he can use to find his way back to me one day.

HotDQ possible spoilers ahead. Our party is tracking the cultists from Waterdeep to their next location, so we got ourselves hired to a caravan guard team and set off on a week-long journey to follow them. We only had two encounters over the 10 days, but one was a troll. We did ok. On arrival at the stopping point, some shit went down. Trying to break into someone's room resulted in me breaking my thieves tools and waking everyone up. Thankfully, I was fast enough to sprint back to our sleeping area before anyone saw me. Someone else was accused, and I nicked some new thieves tools off someone else.

Then, some cultist who had accused me previously of killing her sister (I didn't do it, I swear) challenged me to a duel. I had no choice. People were placing bets before I even agreed to it. Normally, I do really well in the first turn of combat. I have +9 to initiative, so I almost always go first. I also have my broken rogue BS, so I have a possible 8d6+5 total damage for my first hit. BUT, this duel, I rolled two threes (advantage) for my mainhand. Fuck. There went all of my awesome damage. My friends had to stealthily heal me twice throughout the fight. But, I did win.

We called it quits for the night after all that excitement. All-in-all, a good first session back.
How did someone else get blamed? Were you able to procure an alibi, or did you have to do something with the thieve's tools? Either way, that sounds like a really exciting session!

My group had been hired by an ancient green to kill an adult green. They ended up driving the adult out of its lair, only to have the ancient show up shortly after the adult had flown away, with the adult dead in its mouth. When he hired them, he told them that as payment for their killing the adult, he would spare the town up the road. "I am incredibly disappointed in you, mortals... but since I am a generous benefactor, I decided to give you half pay for a job half down, and I only ate all their cattle and a few of their children." The ancient told them he'd be seeing them again, and took off.

So now they're back on the road of their main quest. They've been exploring the ShrineBarrow of Gurri Bloodbeard, a famous dwarf hero. The ShrineBarrow is on a small island that has recently rose out of the sea, and they've been working on getting to the final room, in which Gurri's axe is rumored to be (mechanically this is the Axe of Dwarven Lords). After they fist found the dungeon, they have gotten one clue per room on how to advance to the next room, and so far it has sent them halfway around my game world. They currently have the key to get to the fourth room of the dungeon.

They got sidetracked last session, and are currently exploring an ettin's cave, in which they've found passage to an old dwarven ruin. Hopefully we'll get back on track this week.
